System.Title: sticr copy
System.Description:
Describe the problem/error:
From SCOE Pen-test which is attached:
It is observed that the SQL Server in use, is not configured to utilize few of the security features.
It was noticed that it doesn’t use data in transit encryption.

Expected behavior: Data in transit is forced to be encrypted

Steps to Reproduce:

In "SQL Server Configuration Manager" view "SQL Server Network Configuration" on the left hand side. Double click on "Protocols for MSSQLSERVER" and view "Force Encryption"

When connecting to the SQL Database from SQL Server Management Studio, under the Connection Security header select Encryption Optional. Then once connected right click on the server in the left side pane, select server properties, then on the left hand side of that window select "View Connection Properties". Then observe that under Connection Encrypted is set to "No".

02-Oct-2025/ERyan:
Describe the problem from a development perspective, the potential fix and any workarounds for the problem: Requiring encrypted connections for database connections includes specifying and managing the certificate used for those connections. For local connections, we can leverage the certificate PIC iX is using for inter-process communication. For offloaded SQL instances, this becomes much more complicated, as we need need to manage certificates between the customer-provided SQL host and PIC iX.

Outside of this configuration, an additional layer of security can be added by restricting remote access. This is being tracked by #1246406.

I have split the original STICR in two, as the effort to support this for local SQL instances is very different than to include offloading.
